title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Lahore. Tip #1
body: Sit outside Aitchison or LGS at two o'clock and you've read the whole city. If a Land Cruiser pulls up and nobody gets out of the driver's seat, that's a driver. If a sixteen-year-old gets into a Civic with no licence and zero concern, that's a family that has never had a problem a phone call couldn't fix. It's a sealed deal if the guard opens the gate before the car reaches it because he knows the plate.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 Aitchison walo I'm not naming names.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Lahore. Tip #2
body: Ask what happens after school and listen for the word tutor. Not academy, tutor, who comes to the house, one subject, forty thousand a month. The academy kids are a different tier and both sides know it. It's a sealed deal if that tutor taught the older brother first and has been coming to that house for eleven years.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Lahore. Tip #3
body: June sorts them, because nobody survives Lahore in June. "We're going up to Murree" is one lobby. "We're doing Hunza" is the photograph. "We go to London every year" is the one you're looking for, and it is never called a holiday. It's a sealed deal if there's a flat somewhere they have never once referred to as a hotel.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Lahore. Tip #4
body: Listen to the switching, because in Lahore it runs three ways. Punjabi with the cook, Urdu with the parents, English with friends, none of it planned. If the English has an accent from no country on earth, that's twelve years at the same school. It's a sealed deal if the grandmother speaks the best English in the room and corrects all three languages without looking up.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Lahore. Tip #5
body: Compare the car he drives to the car at home. The son has the loud one, the Civic with the exhaust or a wrapped Vezel. The father drives a 2009 Land Cruiser with a scratch down one side he has never fixed. It costs four times as much. It's a sealed deal if he laughs when you ask about his dad's car, because that laugh is the whole class system.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Lahore. Tip #6
body: Watch how the house talks to the staff, because it's the sharpest tell in the country and nobody says it out loud. New money is loud with staff. Old money is quiet, knows the cook's kids' names, and has paid for a wedding. Neither is admirable. They are completely different. It's a sealed deal if a cook has been there thirty years and the children call him by a title, not a name.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Lahore. Tip #7
body: Ask about university and the plan is already finished. "LUMS, hopefully" is what they tell relatives. Abroad was decided when the kid was fourteen. If they're doing A Levels instead of FSc, they were never staying, and everyone at that table worked that out years ago. It's a sealed deal if a UCAS deadline has caused more household stress than any exam ever did.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Lahore. Tip #8
body: Watch what happens when the light goes, because it doesn't. The generator catches in two seconds and nobody pauses mid-sentence. There's a bore, so a tanker has never been discussed. That is the real privilege and it is completely invisible from inside. It's a sealed deal if a teenager in that house cannot tell you what load-shedding actually means.
